# Audit findings, 2026-10

Full-repository audit at `8e33fb3` for KISS / DRY / SOLID / dead code / false claims / below-floor
compatibility, and for real defects. Every finding was produced by a read-only finder and then given
to a skeptic told to refute it: on facts (does the defect exist as stated) and on regression (what
would the proposal break). Nothing here has been applied yet.

- **confirmed** — no skeptic refuted it; the proposal shown is the verifier's corrected one when it gave one.
- **unverified** — the verification has not finished yet.
- **refuted** — a skeptic showed the claim false or the proposal unsafe; the reason is kept.

Two verification passes, and they are not equally strong. The first gave each finding its own
skeptic (`reality`, `regression` or `combined` below) and refuted 19 of 135. A usage limit
stopped it; the remaining 290 went through one skeptic per batch of up to eight (`batch`), which
refuted 5 and rescued 224 only with a corrected proposal. Read a `batch`-only verdict as weaker
evidence: the tester loop is what proves a card, not this page.

`est` is the finder's estimate of net lines removed (negative adds lines); it is not measured.

### `router-1-3` The document <h1> keeps the previous page's title when the router opens a view node that has no title

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est 1 · changes behaviour

- **Where:** fs-router.js:1044-1047, 1086-1087; reference header.ut:198
- **Claim:** On a full load the server renders .fs-title-main as the node title or else the hostname. navigate() updates it only `if (tmain && node.title)`, so after a client navigation to an untitled view node the screen-reader-only <h1> still names the page that was left. Stock LuCI ships such a node on all three branches: admin/status/nftables/iptables. Its page is opened by `location.href` from nftables.js (a full load), so the client router reaches it through Back: full load of the iptables page, then a menu click (client navigation), then Back (popstate -> navigate). The <h1> then reads the clicked page's title.
- **Proposal:** Apply as written. Declare `const title = node.title ? _(node.title) : '';` once, before line 1044, at navigate()'s top block level so it is still in scope at line 1087. Then: `document.title = title ? titleHost() + ' | ' + title : titleHost();` / `if (tmain) tmain.textContent = title || titleHost();` / `if (live) live.textContent = title;`. Net line saving is about 0-1, not a size win; the value is the parity fix. docs/spa-router.md:470 stays accurate.
- **Original proposal:** Compute it once: `const title = node.title ? _(node.title) : '';` then `document.title = title ? titleHost() + ' | ' + title : titleHost();`, `if (tmain) tmain.textContent = title || titleHost();` and `if (live) live.textContent = title;`. This also replaces the three separate `_(node.title)` evaluations.
- **Verdict (reality): holds.** The bug is real at HEAD and works as described. navigate() writes .fs-title-main only when node.title is set (fs-router.js:1046), and nothing else in the code writes that element. On a full load, header.ut:198 falls back to the hostname. Stock LuCI ships an untitled view node, admin/status/nftables/iptables, on 24.10, 25.12 and master. The router does wire on that page and takes popstate to it as a client navigation, so the <h1> keeps the previous page's title. The proposed fix is correct and ha … Breaks: Nothing functional. The est_lines_saved=1 figure is wrong: the old code is 4 lines plus 1 and the proposal is also 4 lines plus 1, so the net saving is 0.
- **Verdict (regression): holds.** The bug is real. menutree resolveSegs/viewClassFor accept an untitled view node: firstChildOf needs a title, but the direct path lookup does not. So popstate's navigate() reaches admin/status/nftables/iptables and leaves the previous page's <h1> on screen. For titled nodes the proposal gives the same document.title, h1 and live-region text as now. For untitled nodes it changes only the h1, which becomes titleHost(), the same as header.ut:198's server fallback. No gate, test or tool reads the h1 …

### `router-2-1` popstate: the ?query check runs before the fragment check, so a fragment-only change on a page with a query reloads it

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est 0 · changes behaviour

- **Where:** fs-router.js:1424-1438 (query reload at 1427-1430 runs before the fragment guard at 1437-1438), 394 (_curPath = pathname only), 992
- **Claim:** The popstate handler calls location.reload() whenever location.search is non-empty, before it checks whether only the fragment moved. Any same-document fragment navigation on a page reached with a query reloads that page: an <a href="#"> without preventDefault, the theme's own .fs-skip link (href="#maincontent"), or Back over such an entry. Commit 322ee8f added the fragment guard below the query check, so the query case was never covered.
- **Proposal:** Keep the pathname guard and add the search to it. Add `let _curSearch = window.location.search;` at module eval next to _curPath, and `_curSearch = '';` beside `_curPath = pathname;` in navigate(). popstate: `const loc = window.location; if (loc.pathname === _curPath && (!loc.search || loc.search === _curSearch)) return; if (loc.search) { loc.reload(); return; }`, then the existing path. Every case the old code returned on still returns. The only new return is the same pathname with the same boot query, which is the bug. Update docs/spa-router.md lines 90-92 and 115-120.
- **Original proposal:** Track the URL that is on screen, not just its path. Set `_curUrl = location.pathname + location.search` at module eval, keep `_curUrl = pathname` in navigate(), and make the popstate handler's first check `if (location.pathname + location.search === _curUrl) return;`. The `location.search` reload check goes after it. One moved block and one renamed variable.
- **Verdict (batch): holds.** Дефект подтверждён: в popstate проверка search (1427) стоит раньше fragment-guard (1437), поэтому фрагментная навигация на странице с ?query перезагружает её. Реальные триггеры: package-manager (Reset href=#, активный таб в handleMode без preventDefault) и собственный .fs-skip href=#maincontent. Предложение в текущем виде регрессирует: weechat/servers.js (25.12/master) через replaceState убирает ?server= уже после eval модуля. Тогда _curUrl=P?server=x, после фрагмента URL=P, сравнение не совпада … Breaks: luci-app-weechat ?server=X (25.12/master): после replaceState фрагмент или skip-link перерисовывает вид через navigate()

### `router-2-2` commitStage() throws away the incoming page's own ui.addNotification banners (regression from staging)

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est 0 · changes behaviour

- **Where:** fs-router.js:807-828 (commitStage calls sweepAround at 811), 867-882 (the #maincontent alert-message sweep), 1187-1240 (stage renders before commit)
- **Claim:** ui.addNotification() inserts into #maincontent, and many views call it from load() or render(). With staging, those views run before commitStage(). sweepAround() then discards every .alert-message child of #maincontent, which now includes the banners the incoming page just created. A full load shows them. While staging, they also show above the outgoing page. When the sweep was added (bbe5cbd) it ran synchronously in navigate() before the require. edf09ee moved it into commitStage, after the render.
- **Proposal:** Use the snapshot variant. In navigate()'s teardown, right before stageView(), record `const outgoingBanners = mainHost ? Array.from(mainHost.children).filter((c) => c.classList.contains('alert-message')) : [];` and store it on the stage object. In commitStage, sweepAround keeps the .fs-content sibling sweep and discards only stage.banners (`stage.banners.forEach((b) => { if (b.parentNode) discard(b); })`) instead of every #maincontent .alert-message. A superseded render's banners are still in #maincontent at the next navigation's teardown, so they are captured and swept. Known ceiling: a banner the outgoing page adds after teardown, from an in-flight RPC, survives. Update the sweepAround comment and docs/spa-router.md.
- **Original proposal:** Split sweepAround(). The .fs-content-sibling half stays in commitStage(). The #maincontent .alert-message half moves into navigate()'s teardown block, just before stageView() (about line 1187), so it removes only banners that existed before the incoming render started. Alternative: snapshot those banners into `stage` at teardown and discard exactly that list at commit.
- **Verdict (batch): holds.** Дефект подтверждён: addNotification на 24.10, 25.12 и master вставляет баннер в #maincontent. Рендер в стейдже идёт до commitStage, и sweepAround при коммите удаляет баннеры входящей страницы (например 'Legacy rules detected' из nftables render). Регрессию внёс edf09ee: в bbe5cbd sweep выполнялся в navigate() до require. Основное предложение (sweep в teardown перед stageView) нарушает задокументированное правило окна staging: уходящая страница сохраняет вид до коммита. Удаление баннеров сверху # … Breaks: основное предложение (sweep в teardown) уберёт баннеры уходящей страницы в начале окна staging и сдвинет контент, который читают

### `router-2-3` Back resets nothing when there is no non-zero offset to restore, so the sidebar layout opens the page at the outgoing page's offset

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est 0 · changes behaviour

- **Where:** fs-router.js:1232-1238 (reset only `if (push)`), 455 (restoreScroll returns on {win:0,main:0}), claims at 452 ('left at the top') and 1062
- **Claim:** On a popstate commit the scrollers are never reset. restoreScroll() returns at once when the saved offsets are both 0, or when nothing was saved. #maincontent is the scroller in the sidebar layout and it survives the dom.content() swap, so the restored page keeps the scrollTop the reader had on the page they left, clamped to the new height. Example: A left at the top, open B, scroll B to 2000, press Back: A opens at 2000. The comment at 452 says such a page is 'left at the top'. That is false.
- **Proposal:** In the commit .then: `const sc = document.getElementById('maincontent'); const r = restoreTo || {}; if (push || !r.win) window.scrollTo(0, 0); if (sc && (push || !r.main)) sc.scrollTo(0, 0); if (r.win || r.main) restoreScroll(restoreTo, gen);`. Each axis the restore does not carry is reset, which is safe because onScroll returns early for an axis with pos 0. The axis being restored is never reset. The early return at 455 may be dropped. Fix the comments at 452 and 1062 and the 'Scroll' section of docs/spa-router.md.
- **Original proposal:** In the commit .then, replace `if (push) {reset}` and `if (restoreTo) restoreScroll(...)` with: `if (restoreTo && (restoreTo.win || restoreTo.main)) restoreScroll(restoreTo, gen); else { window.scrollTo(0, 0); if (sc) sc.scrollTo(0, 0); }`. Then drop the early return at 455, since the caller now decides. Do not reset before a pending restore: the async scroll event from the reset would cancel it in onScroll.
- **Verdict (batch): holds.** Дефект подтверждён: при popstate-коммите скроллеры не сбрасываются (только при push). restoreScroll сразу выходит при {0,0} или null. В sidebar-лейауте #maincontent переживает dom.content(), поэтому A открывается на offset B (с clamp). Комментарии на 452 и 1062 ложные. Предложение корректно: сброс идёт только когда restore не запланирован, onScroll привязан к оси, поэтому самоотмены нет. Его можно уточнить посбросом по осям: ось, которую pos не несёт, сбрасывать безопасно (onScroll её игнорирует …

### `router-2-4` Fragment history entries are never adopted, so the outgoing offset is saved under the wrong entry and Back cannot restore it

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est -1 · changes behaviour

- **Where:** fs-router.js:1437-1438 (fragment branch returns without adoptEntry), 431-436, 440-447, 1442-1449
- **Claim:** A fragment navigation, such as an app's href="#" tab without preventDefault (filemanager, package-manager) or the skip link, creates a new history entry whose state is null. The popstate fragment branch returns without adoptEntry(), so _curId still names the previous entry. The next click's saveScroll() records the offset under that old id. On Back, the browser lands on the fragment entry, adoptEntry() stamps it with a fresh id, the lookup misses, and the offset is lost. Together with the scroll-reset finding, the page then opens at the outgoing page's offset.
- **Proposal:** In the popstate early-return branch call adoptEntry() before returning, using router-2-1's corrected condition: `if (loc.pathname === _curPath && (!loc.search || loc.search === _curSearch)) { adoptEntry(); return; }`. Update the 'Scroll' section of docs/spa-router.md.
- **Original proposal:** Call adoptEntry() in the fragment branch before returning. Combined with the query-check fix this becomes `if (location.pathname + location.search === _curUrl) { adoptEntry(); return; }`.
- **Verdict (batch): holds.** Дефект подтверждён: фрагментная навигация создаёт запись с state null. Ветка fragment в popstate возвращается без adoptEntry, поэтому _curId остаётся от предыдущей записи. Следующий клик сохраняет offset под старым id, а Back на фрагментную запись получает новый id и промахивается. Повторный клик по href=# (replace) тоже обнуляет state, и adoptEntry в ветке переклеит id. Предложение (adoptEntry() перед return) корректно: replaceState с тем же location.href не скроллит и не мешает hashchange. Оши …

### `router-2-5` A superseded navigation makes the next one spare the wrong page's foreign sheets: `leaving` is taken from L.env at click time

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est 1 · changes behaviour

- **Where:** fs-router.js:997-999 (leaving = L.env.dispatchpath at click), 1023-1024, 1185 (scopeToCurrentPage(rsegs, leaving)), 810
- **Claim:** `leaving` is meant to be the page still on screen, whose sheets must stay lit during staging. It is read from L.env.dispatchpath, which the previous navigate() already re-pointed at click time. Sequence: on A, click B, then click C before B commits. Nav C spares B, a page that was never shown, and disables A's page-owned foreign sheets while A is still the visible page for C's whole staging window.
- **Proposal:** As proposed: declare `let _shown = null;` at module level, set `_shown = (L.env.dispatchpath || []).slice();` in seed(), and set `_shown = rsegs.slice();` right after commitStage() (after the gen check). Teardown calls `sheets.scopeToCurrentPage(rsegs, _shown)`. Delete the `leaving` capture and its comment, and update the `scopeToCurrentPage(rsegs, leaving)` mention in docs/spa-router.md (around line 241).
- **Original proposal:** Keep the committed page in one variable. Set `let _shown = (L.env.dispatchpath || []).slice()` in seed(), set `_shown = rsegs` in the commit .then right after commitStage(), and call `sheets.scopeToCurrentPage(rsegs, _shown)` in the teardown. Delete the click-time `leaving` capture and its comment (997-999).
- **Verdict (batch): holds.** Дефект подтверждён: leaving берётся из L.env.dispatchpath в момент клика, а предыдущий navigate() уже переставил его на свою цель. Сценарий A -> B (не закоммичен) -> C: в teardown C вызывается scopeToCurrentPage(C, B). fs-sheets выключает все owned-листы с owner не равным C и не равным B, то есть листы A, пока A на экране. Предложение с _shown (seed, затем после commitStage) корректно. seed() всегда вызывается до wire() (menu-footstrap-common:371/384). При superseded-навигации _shown не меняется …

### `router-2-6` Progress bar: the show-delay and the fade cleanup share one timer slot, so the bar can stick in data-state=done and later run backwards

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est -1 · changes behaviour

- **Where:** fs-router.js:895, 911-926
- **Claim:** progressEnd() stores its 300 ms fade cleanup in _progressTimer, and progressStart() clears _progressTimer. If a navigation starts inside that 300 ms window and finishes in under 150 ms, progressEnd() sees state 'done' (not 'active') and returns. No timer is left to remove 'done'. The next slow navigation then goes done -> active, i.e. scaleX(1) -> scaleX(.8) over 2 s per 20-shell.css:505-514, so the bar appears full width and shrinks.
- **Proposal:** Only the separate timer: `let _fadeTimer = 0;` and in progressEnd() `window.clearTimeout(_fadeTimer); _fadeTimer = window.setTimeout(() => { if (bar.dataset.state === 'done') delete bar.dataset.state; }, 300);`. progressStart() keeps clearing only _progressTimer. Do not add the delete in the non-active branch. Record the residual case as its own finding: a slow nav started <150 ms after the previous one ended activates from 'done'. The root fix there is at activation (reset from 'done' before 'active'), but it needs a style flush, which goes against the 'composited only' intent in 20-shell.css:492-495, so it has to be measured first.
- **Original proposal:** Give the fade cleanup its own timer (`_fadeTimer`) that progressStart() does not cancel. Also, in progressEnd()'s non-active branch, delete a leftover 'done' instead of returning with it in place.
- **Verdict (batch): holds.** Дефект на HEAD есть. progressStart() гасит 300-мс таймер очистки, потому что он лежит в том же _progressTimer. Если следующая навигация короче 150 мс, progressEnd() видит 'done' и выходит, и 'done' остаётся. Следующая медленная навигация переводит полосу done->active, то есть scaleX(1)->(.8): полоса идёт назад. Отдельный _fadeTimer чинит этот случай сам по себе. Вторая часть предложения (удалять 'done' в ветке non-active) — лишняя страховка. По правилу «один механизм» она не ship-ится, да ещё и … Breaks: the second half (delete 'done' in progressEnd's non-active branch) is a redundant spare under _fadeTimer and cuts a running fade short: a fast nav inside 100 ms of the previous end makes a still-opaque bar vanish instantly

### `router-1-1` Stop L.Poll before pausing/sweeping intervals: drops pollTickId, the private L.Poll.timer read and the second visibilitychange listener

**confirmed** · simplification · risk medium · est 90

- **Where:** fs-router.js:37-40 (IIFE + __fsIntervalsHooked guard), 69-98 (hide path keep logic), 100-125 (pollTickId), 126-131 (clearViewIntervals keep), 139-146 (warnPollUnreadable/_pollWarned), 1144-1156 (navigate teardown order), 1474-1501 (wireVisibility/_visWired), 1512 (export); menu-footstrap-common.js:385
- **Claim:** The `keep` exclusion exists only because L.Poll's tick sits in the interval registry when a sweep/pause runs, and that is purely an ordering artefact. In navigate() it is already always null: queue emptied, stop(), then start() on an empty queue arms no timer, so active() is false before clearViewIntervals(). On hide it is needed only because wireVisibility's listener (registered later) stops the poll after the pause listener ran. Two listeners on the same event with an implicit order dependency, plus a read of private L.Poll.timer and a 'cannot tell apart, pause nothing' degraded mode, all go away if the poll is stopped first.
- **Proposal:** Apply as proposed (top-level hooks, no IIFE or __fsIntervalsHooked, window.__fsViewIntervals = new Map(); one visibilitychange listener, all in try/catch: on hide `_pollWasActive = L.Poll.active(); if (_pollWasActive) L.Poll.stop();`, then pause every live entry; on show re-arm paused entries, then `if (_pollWasActive && !_expired) L.Poll.start()`; clearViewIntervals = clear every key; navigate = `L.Poll.queue.length = 0; L.Poll.stop(); clearViewIntervals(); L.Poll.start();`). Delete pollTickId, warnPollUnreadable, _pollWarned, wireVisibility, _visWired and the export. In the same change: delete menu-footstrap-common.js:385; reword fs-router.js:172 into a standalone 'private shape: do nothing, once, loudly' rule; replace the interval-pause tick test with a luci.js-shaped Poll test that asserts L.Poll.active()===false while hidden, exactly one tick after N hide/show, and that L.Poll.stop() leaves only view timers; keep active() in the upstream-contract poll-alias probe and drop only the timer half; update the spa-parity messages, docs/spa-router.md and both CHANGELOGs; call it a small behaviour change (hide now also pauses the poll before chrome init finishes).
- **Original proposal:** Replace lines 32-146 with: the two hooks at top level (no IIFE, no __fsIntervalsHooked; `window.__fsViewIntervals = new Map()` kept for spa-parity), one visibilitychange listener that does L.Poll.stop() first on hide and L.Poll.start() last on show (keeping the manual-pause and !_expired rules from wireVisibility), and `function clearViewIntervals() { _viewIntervals.forEach((s, id) => window.clearInterval(id)); }`. Delete pollTickId, warnPollUnreadable, _pollWarned, wireVisibility, _visWired, the `wireVisibility` export and menu-footstrap-common.js:385. In navigate: `L.Poll.queue.length = 0; L.Poll.stop(); clearViewIntervals(); L.Poll.start();` (the `if (L.Poll && L.Poll.queue)` guard is unreachable behind CONTRACT_REST's L.Poll.queue check).
- **Verdict (reality): holds.** The core claim holds at HEAD. In navigate, queue=0, stop() and then start() leave the Poll with no timer, so pollTickId() is null when the sweep runs. On hide, `keep` is needed only because the eval-time pause listener runs before wireVisibility's stop(). With stop() first, the tick leaves the registry through the hook. A real luci.js Poll from 24.10 and from master gives the same results on HEAD and on the patched copy. ### `router-2-7` classLoaded()'s dotted walk is effectively dead: luci.js never attaches nested classes at that path; replace with _seen and drop the L.Class contract entry

### `select-1-1` Enhanced <select> shows its options in a different order from the native one (integer keys hoisted)

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est 0 · changes behaviour

- **Where:** fs-select.js:21-25 (readChoices builds a plain object), fs-select.js:94-97 (`sort: false`)
- **Claim:** enhance() passes the options as a plain object with `sort: false`. ui.Dropdown then orders them by Object.keys(), and Object.keys() puts integer-like keys first in ascending order. Any select whose native order is not ascending-integer-first gets reordered. On stock System > Logging, 'Log output level' (values 8..1) shows reversed, 'Cron Log Level' (7,9,5) shows as 5,7,9, and a '' placeholder placed first moves after numeric options.
- **Proposal:** Apply as written: fs-select.js:95 `sort: Array.from(sel.options, (o) => o.value),`. Only if the maintainer wants to keep today's merging of duplicate values: `sort: [...new Set(Array.from(sel.options, (o) => o.value))]`. That diverges from native, so the plain form is preferred.
- **Original proposal:** Replace `sort: false` with `sort: Array.from(sel.options, (o) => o.value)`, which is ui.Dropdown's documented explicit-order form. readChoices stays as the label map.
- **Verdict (reality): holds.** Reproduced. fs-select.js:94-97 passes `sort: false` with a plain-object map from readChoices (21-25), so ui.Dropdown.render keeps Object.keys order, which puts integer-like keys first in ascending order (24.10 ui.js:1066-1071, the same in 25.12/master at 1096-1101). The native ui.Select uses the form's keylist order (form.js 24.10:4355). Typeahead (fs-select.js:865) walks the li elements in DOM order, so it inherits the wrong order too. The proposal fixes this: the array form of `sort` is docume … Breaks: As written, with duplicate option values (form.js value() does not dedupe keylist; a hand-built select from a third-party app can have duplicates) the proposal renders duplicate li elements with the same data-value, both labelled with readChoices' last-wins label. Today one li is rendered.
- **Verdict (regression): holds.** The bug is real. At fs-select.js:94-97, ui.Dropdown gets a plain object with sort:false, so its keys come out in Object.keys() order, which puts integer-like keys first in ascending order. The native <select> follows form.js keylist order instead. ui.Dropdown's render logic is the same on 24.10, 25.12 and master. Passing the native option values as the sort array makes the dropdown match native order in every case I simulated. Nothing in the repo depends on the old order: no test, gate, gallery … Breaks: Not a loss, but visible: a select with duplicate option values (form.js value() does not dedupe keylist) now shows the duplicate rows the native select shows, where today they are merged into one. Each duplicate row uses the label of the last duplicate, because readChoices keeps one label per value. Selection still works: ui.Dropdown.setValues toggles every match and the last one stays selected.

### `select-2-4` wireActivate activates on every keydown auto-repeat, and Space on keydown

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est -1 · changes behaviour

Holding it on a clickable indicator pill (fs-chrome.js:508 -> ui.showIndicator's handler) toggles polling repeatedly. A native button and the W3C-APG button pattern activate on Space keyup, once.
- **Proposal:** fs-widgets.js wireActivate: `if (ev.key !== 'Enter' && ev.key !== ' ') return; ev.preventDefault(); if (!ev.repeat) activate();`. menu-footstrap.js wireSpaceKey: `if (ev.key !== ' ') return; ev.preventDefault(); if (!ev.repeat) link.click();`. preventDefault должен оставаться на каждом keydown, включая повторы, иначе удержание Space прокручивает страницу. Минимальный фикс в виде «`if (ev.repeat) return;` первой строкой» вносит регрессию: повторные keydown от Space больше не получают preventDefault, и при удержании Space на сфокусированном span/a[role=button] страница (или сайдбар) начинает прокручиваться. Спасается тем, … Breaks: minimal fix as written (repeat check as the first line) skips preventDefault on repeat Space keydowns, so holding Space scrolls the page or the sidebar

**confirmed** · dead-code · risk low · est 6

In the attributeFilter, 'value' and 'selected' only produce records relevant() drops. A select has no value content attribute, 'selected' lives on <option>/<li> targets, and the check accepts only tagName SELECT. The main 'selected' traffic is ui.Dropdown's own li writes on every pick.
- **Proposal:** Apply as proposed: - `return fit.touches(mutations, 'select.cbi-input-select');` - `attributeFilter: [ 'disabled' ]` - Collapse the loop to `for (const m of mutations) if (m.target.tagName === 'SELECT') return true;` and keep the replaceChildren/option-rebuild reason as an inline comment, because it is the non-obvious half. - Fix the stale comments: 820-823 says "three" querySelectorAll but scan has two; drop 838-839; reword 965-966 to say a `disabled` flip mutates no childList. - Keep the comment at 64-71 (it is still accurate). Optional follow-up, a separate defect fix rather than part of this change: accept `m.target.closest?.('select')` so option- and optgroup-level rebuilds re-key the widget. If you do that, `'value'` would come back for option.value writes, but only with evidence that some app actually does that.
- **Original proposal:** `return fit.touches(mutations, 'select.cbi-input-select');`. Use `attributeFilter: [ 'disabled' ]`. With only disabled-attribute and childList records left, the loop body collapses to `if (m.target.tagName === 'SELECT') return true;`. Trim the stale comments.
- **Verdict (combined): holds.** This holds at HEAD 8e33fb3. scan() (fs-select.js:933-936) only enhances and resyncs selects. Table tagging moved to fit.add() in c1cfbe4, and the same commit widened relevant() to `.table`, so a table added with no select in it wakes a scan with nothing to do. resyncValues already runs on that same childList batch through fs-fit. `selected` is only ever written on `<li>` (ui.js 24.10:1159-1469, widgets.js:203), and relevant() accepts only a SELECT target, so those records are dropped. No upstrea … Breaks: Nothing functional. The only wakeups lost are a value attribute on a SELECT, which no upstream code writes and which does not change sel.value, and a `.table` added with no select in it, where scan has nothing to do and fs-fit's resyncValues already runs on that batch. The one remaining gap is a coincidence: an `<optgroup>` child rebuild, or an option's text/value changed in place, used to get re-keyed only when it landed in the same batch as a table addition. It was never handled on purpose: relevant() drops OPTION and OPTGROUP targets before and after this change, so this is a latent gap that already exists, not a regression.

### `select-1-9` Header-row lookup spelled three ways; shapeOf() has drifted and misses <thead> tables

**confirmed** · duplication · risk low · est 3

- **Where:** fs-select.js:220 (tagDataTables head), fs-select.js:255 and 282 (identical titleRow ternary), fs-select.js:505-508 (shapeOf)

It ignores `thead` and headerRow(), so for any `<table><thead><tr>` table (e.g. luci-mod-dashboard) the shape is the thead's child count, always '1', or a <caption>'s. The column-count half of the slot signature is blind for exactly the foreign tables tagDataTables recognises.

In fs-select.js, add `function headOf(t) { return t.querySelector('.tr.table-titles, .tr.cbi-section-table-titles, thead') || headerRow(t); }` and `const titleRow = (head) => (head.firstElementChild && head.firstElementChild.tagName === 'TR') ? head.firstElementChild : head;`. Move the labelCells comment at lines 279-281 onto titleRow. tagDataTables uses `const head = headOf(t)`. adoptMarkup uses `for (const c of titleRow(head).children)`. labelCells uses `[ ...titleRow(head).children ]`. shapeOf becomes `const head = headOf(t); return String(head ? titleRow(head).children.length : 0);`. Each table then has one head lookup and one title-row rule, and that also fixes the row-count shape for non-adopted parsed `<table><tr class=tr><th>` tables.
- **Original proposal:** Add one `const HEAD = '.tr.table-titles, .tr.cbi-section-table-titles, thead'` and one `titleRow(head)` helper. tagDataTables uses `t.querySelector(HEAD) || headerRow(t)`. adoptMarkup and labelCells call titleRow(head). shapeOf returns `String(head ? titleRow(head).children.length : 0)` using the same lookup.
- **Verdict (combined): holds.** The defect is real at HEAD, but the finding has its example and its labels wrong. luci-mod-dashboard builds `<thead>` with E() and puts the `<th>`s straight inside it, so shapeOf already returns 3 there. The tables that really fail are stock thead>tr tables: luci-app-lldpd's filter table (bare `<table>`, adopted, gets no `.tr.table-titles`) and the filemanager table. A `<caption>` first gives 0. A parsed, non-adopted `<tr class=tr><th>` table gives its ROW count, which is a second drift the find … Breaks: Nothing functional. The finding mislabels it: behaviour_change=false is wrong (the slot-cache key changes for thead>tr, caption-first and non-adopted parsed headerRow tables, which is the fix itself), and est_lines_saved=3 is about 0 (two helper lines added, two loop lines merged).; The finding's cited example (luci-mod-dashboard) is not affected; the affected stock tables are luci-app-lldpd's filter table and luci-app-filemanager's file table.

It is called once per unanswered table inside the forEach, interleaved with applyDecision()'s class writes, so from the second table on each call reads a layout the previous iteration invalidated.
- **Proposal:** In fitTables(), declare `let cw;` above the forEach. In the scrolling branch, write `if (!known && cw === undefined) cw = chrome.contentWidth();` and then `stack: cw < CRAMPED`. Use a plain `if`, not `??=`. Change the comments at fs-select.js:6, 521-522, 524 and 541-542 to: one window-width read per pass, which forces layout only on classic-scrollbar engines (overlay-scrollbar phones skip the flush). In the same edit, fix the 'costs nothing' wording at fs-chrome.js:592-596 and docs/chrome.md:120-122, and the 'WITHOUT reading layout' wording at tools/live-audit.mjs:154. Expect about 0 net code lines saved; the value is one forced layout per pass instead of N, plus accurate comments. If code churn is not wanted, a comment-only fix is the zero-risk minimum.

In fs-select.js, the mid-scroll branch calls chrome.contentWidth() once for each table that has no slot answer, and applyDecision() class writes happen between those calls. contentWidth() reads documentElement.clientWidth every time (fs-chrome.js:598). Chromium and Gecko both force style and layout for that read unless the scrollbars are overlay scrollbars. So on classic-scrollbar desktops, N unanswered tables cost N forced layouts. Overlay-scrollbar phones ski … Breaks: As written, the proposal contradicts itself: it asks for a read that is both 'lazily once' and 'before any applyDecision write'. A lazy read can come after an earlier known table's write. This does not matter, because the poll tick has already dirtied layout, so on classic scrollbars the first read costs one forced layout either way. The current code already judges the first table on that width, and fit.deferMeasurement() schedules a full measured pass that corrects it. No functionality is lost.; If only fs-select's comments are fixed, fs-chrome.js:592-596, docs/chrome.md:95/120-122 and tools/live-audit.mjs:154 still say the read is free or not a layout read. They need correcting too.

### `select-1-3` Enhanced select replaces an accessible combobox with a role-less div; its aria-label lands on a role that prohibits naming

**refuted** · bug · risk medium · est -10 · changes behaviour

- **Claim:** Every CBI <select> is hidden from assistive tech (display:none + aria-hidden). It is replaced by ui.Dropdown's `div.cbi-dropdown`, which has no role, no expanded state and no option roles on 24.10, 25.12 or master. The name enhance() writes sits on a generic element, where ARIA 1.2 prohibits aria-label (axe flags this as aria-prohibited-attr). Whether a screen reader announces it depends on the browser, and the control is never announced as a list box. Stock themes leave the native select, so this is an a11y regression on every ListValue.
- **Proposal:** Main fix, upstream: open an openwrt/luci PR against ui.Dropdown. - In render() and bind(): give sb role=combobox, aria-haspopup=listbox and aria-expanded=false. Give the ul role=listbox and each li role=option. - Set aria-selected wherever the 'selected' attribute is toggled. - Flip aria-expanded in openDropdown() (ui.js 24.10:1265) and in closeDropdown() (:1379). This also fixes stock's own role-less dropdowns: network and zone pickers, DynamicList, Combobox. Interim theme fix, only if the maintainer wants one. All of it goes in fs-select.js: 1. In enhance(), right after dd.render(), write the static ARIA: - node: role=combobox, aria-haspopup=listbox, aria-expanded=false - node.querySelector('ul'): role=listbox - each li: role=option, with aria-selected taken from li.hasAttribute('selected') This is safe because fs-select passes no create option, so the li set is fixed for the life of the node. 2. In the existing body observer callback (fs-select.js:961), add 'open' to the attributeFilter at :967. Then, before relevant(), add a branch that handles two cases with widgets.syncAttr: - an 'open' mutation on a .cbi-dropdown carrying the enhanced mark: mirror it to aria-expanded - a 'selected' mutation on its li: mirror it to aria-selected 3. Either make fs-fit's _moTabs callback (fs-fit.js:609-611) skip r.target.matches('.cbi-dropdown'), or accept one fit run() per open or close. Measure that cost before choosing. teardown() needs nothing new, because node.remove() drops it all.
- **Original proposal:** Fix the root cause upstream: an openwrt/luci PR adding role=combobox, aria-expanded and aria-haspopup=listbox on sb, role=listbox on the ul and role=option with aria-selected on each li, in ui.Dropdown. Interim theme fix: in enhance(), set role=combobox and aria-haspopup=listbox on node, then mirror aria-expanded from [open] by adding 'open' to the existing body observer's attributeFilter (no new observer).
- **Verdict (reality): holds.** The core defect exists at HEAD 8e33fb3. enhance() hides every single, enabled select.cbi-input-select inside .cbi-value(-field) (fs-select.js:110, :128) and puts ui.Dropdown's div in its place. ### `sheets-1-1` @import'd rules escape the chrome fence (fenceRules never follows CSSImportRule.styleSheet)

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est -2 · changes behaviour

- **Where:** fs-sheets.js:374-390 (fenceRules recurses only via r.cssRules), fs-sheets.js:239-243 (judgeSheet DOES follow r.styleSheet), fs-sheets.js:628-637 (<style> path: no wrap, fence, claimOwner), fs-sheets.js:399-407 (fenceImported fences cssRules[0].styleSheet only, no nested import), false comments fs-sheets.js:290-292 and 433-435
- **Claim:** judgeSheet counts rules behind an @import, but fenceRules only descends r.cssRules, and a CSSImportRule has no cssRules (it exposes styleSheet). An app <style> carrying @import is judged invasive, then left unwrapped because textIsSheet is false (replaceSync drops @import), its imported rules stay unfenced and unlayered, and claimOwner marks it contained so documentPoisoned ignores it. Unlayered imported rules beat every layered chrome rule on that page. The same gap applies to a nested @import inside a re-hosted <link>. The comments at 290-292 (an @import sheet is unattributed and spends the document) and 433-435 (the fence still holds the chrome without the wrap) are false for this shape.

Do not let fenceRules' inner try stand in for 'not ready'. 3) Comments: say imported rules are fenced only if their sheet is loaded when the fence runs. On Blink/WebKit, an import still loading then (a <style> re-hosted on an earlier top-level rule; a nested import in a shim) stays unfenced on its own page. claimOwner still disables it on other pages. Optional follow-up as its own change: fence imports from the element's `load` event. Measured: on a <style>, load fires only after nested @imports are readable in all three engines. That would also cover scenarios B and C.
- **Original proposal:** In fenceRules, add the branch judgeSheet already has: `if (r.styleSheet) { try { fenceRules(r.styleSheet.cssRules, names); } catch (e) { /* unreadable: unfenced */ } }`. Then fenceImported can call `fenceRules(styleEl.sheet.cssRules, names)` once the import is readable, instead of picking cssRules[0].styleSheet by hand, and that also covers nested imports. Correct the two comments.
- **Verdict (reality): holds.** The core claim holds at HEAD. CSSImportRule exposes styleSheet and has no cssRules, and fenceRules (fs-sheets.js:374-390) only descends r.cssRules. replaceSync drops @import, so textIsSheet returns false and no wrap happens. claimOwner runs anyway (line 637), so documentPoisoned skips the sheet. The proposed branch is correct and safe, and it fixes the case where the import is already loaded. It is incomplete in three ways. Imports still loading at rehost time stay unfenced, because fsLayered st … Breaks: Nothing regresses. It fences only imports already loaded when the fence runs. A <style> with @import plus a top-level invasive rule gets judged before the import loads, then owned, and its imports stay unfenced on Blink/WebKit (same as HEAD). Nested imports in a <link> shim get fenced on Gecko only. fenceImported must keep its readiness check: dropping it leaves the whole <link> shim unfenced on Blink/WebK … Breaks: Only if fenceImported's readiness check is dropped (calling fenceRules(styleEl.sheet.cssRules) as soon as styleEl.sheet exists and relying on fenceRules' inner try/skip): Blink and WebKit then leave the whole re-hosted <link> shim unfenced, because cssRules[0].styleSheet is null at insertion. HEAD fences the shim's own rules.; Comment risk: rewriting fs-sheets.js:290-292/433-435 to say @import sheets are fenced or contained would be a new false claim. ### `sheets-2-2` fenceImported polls rAF against a 1 s deadline for a network event; shim's native load event fits

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est 16 · changes behaviour

- **Where:** fs-sheets.js:392-415 (fenceImported, deadline + console.error), fs-sheets.js:604 (Date.now()+1000), fs-sheets.js:595-596 and 396-398 (claim 're-fetch is a cache hit'), fs-sheets.js:701-710 + 778-779 (dedupe may delete the shim being polled)
- **Claim:** On the first visit the shim's @import joins the original link's in-flight network fetch, so it is not a cache hit. When that fetch takes longer than 1 s (a slow or remote admin link, the 117 KB openclash sheet), or the tab is hidden (no rAF), the deadline passes. The re-hosted sheet then stays unfenced for the life of the document, and every later pass skips it as fsLayered. The loop also keeps polling a shim that dedupeViewSheets has removed, whose .sheet is null, and then logs a false 'stays unfenced' error.
- **Proposal:** `function fenceImported(s, names) { const fence = () => { try { fenceRules(s.sheet.cssRules[0].styleSheet.cssRules, names); return true; } catch (e) { return false; } }; if (!fence()) s.addEventListener('load', () => { if (!fence()) console.error('footstrap: the re-hosted @import loaded but could not be read — the sheet stays unfenced and may repaint the chrome on this page.', s); }, { once: true }); }`. Call it as `fenceImported(s, universe.names)`. Drop the deadline and its comment, rewrite the header comment to say why it waits for load (a network fetch, not a frame), drop the hidden-tab sentence, and fix the 'cache hit' comments at 595-596 and 604. A 404 fires `error`, which has nothing to fence, so it needs no handler.
- **Original proposal:** Replace the rAF/deadline loop with one sync attempt plus the element's event: `const fence = () => { try { fenceRules(s.sheet.cssRules[0].styleSheet.cssRules, names); return true; } catch (e) { return false; } }; if (!fence()) s.addEventListener('load', fence, { once: true });`. Drop the deadline, the console.error and their comments. A removed shim never fires load.

### `sheets-2-5` SVG cleaning deletes content that renders and is inert in image mode: <style> and data: bitmaps

**confirmed** · bug · risk medium · est 13 · changes behaviour

- **Claim:** Two cases. (1) Adobe Illustrator's SVG export puts presentation in an internal <style> (`.cls-1{fill:none;stroke:…}`). (1) Take 'style' out of PAT_BAD_TAGS, but remove a <style> element (counted in `elements`) when `_externalStyleRef(el.textContent)` is true: @import, expression( or any url( not starting with #. This is the same rule the attribute already follows, so an Illustrator `.cls-1{fill:none;stroke:#000}` or `fill:url(#grad)` survives byte-identical. (4) Add tests: an Illustrator <style> survives untouched; `<style>@import url(//x)</style>` is still removed; `<image href="data:image/png…">` survives; `<a href="data:text/html…">` is still stripped. - **Original proposal:** Remove 'style' from PAT_BAD_TAGS and the `(data|blob|about):` clause at 291, delete the comment paragraphs at 108-112 and 129-136, and add two tests (an internal <style> survives; a data: <image> survives). Both removals are inert in image mode and under the CGI's CSP default-src 'none'; sandbox. 49902b7 itself calls the check 'a hint, not a defence'. But the proposal as written is incoherent. A <style> ele … Breaks: as written: a <style> element can carry the url()/@import the style-attribute check strips, making that security-reviewed check moot; as written: data: survives on <a>/<use> hrefs too, not just bitmaps; comment cross-references at fs-assets.js:84, 87-88, 120-121, 287-289 left stale

### `sheets-1-3` Sticky invasive-verdict cache (_invasive + invasiveSheet wrapper) is dead mechanics

**confirmed** · dead-code · risk low · est 28

- **Where:** fs-sheets.js:171-200 (_invasive, invasiveSheet wrapper, readable try), fs-sheets.js:205-208 (try around el.sheet), fs-sheets.js:302-307 (documentPoisoned judges before checking _owner/_silenced)
- **Claim:** The cache exists so a fenced sheet is not re-judged as clean (commit d3c48c7, when the fence named a class and the judge was a themeHit test). That reason no longer holds, for two reasons. (1) Fencing cannot change a verdict: CHROME_FENCE carries no class or id, and stripPseudoArgs strips it. (2) Every element the cache can hold (readable and invasive) is marked fsLayered and then either silenced (LINK, line 602) or owned (STYLE, line 637). rehostInvasiveSheets skips fsLayered (647) and documentPoisoned excludes owned and silenced elements (306). So the cached `true` is never what decides an outcome. The wrapper's `try { el.sheet }` also guards nothing: the LinkStyle.sheet getter never throws, per the CSSOM spec.
- **Proposal:** Same as proposed, already applied in scratch/sheets13/fs-sheets.js and lint-clean. Delete lines 171-200 (`_invasive` and the wrapper), rename `judgeSheet` to `invasiveSheet` with `const sheet = el.sheet; if (!sheet) return true;`, and in `documentPoisoned` put `!_owner.has(el) && !_silenced.has(el)` before `invasiveSheet(el, names)`. This saves 32 lines (claimed 28). Strictly, there is a minimal behaviour change in the never-re-hosted edge case above, and it moves toward the correct answer.
- **Original proposal:** Delete `_invasive` and the invasiveSheet wrapper (171-200), rename judgeSheet to invasiveSheet, and make its first lines `const sheet = el.sheet; if (!sheet) return true;`. In documentPoisoned, test containment before judging: `outlivesPage(el) && (!names || (!_owner.has(el) && !_silenced.has(el) && invasiveSheet(el, names)))`. This also stops a full CSSOM walk of every contained sheet on each navigation.
- **Verdict (combined): holds.** The claim holds at HEAD. Every route that writes to `_invasive` ends in either `silence()` (LINK, fs-sheets.js:602) or `claimOwner()` (STYLE, :637). `rehostInvasiveSheets` skips any element marked fsLayered (:647), and `documentPoisoned` excludes owned and silenced elements (:306), so the cached `true` never decides an outcome. Fencing also leaves the verdict unchanged. The cache existed only because, in d3c48c7, `documentPoisoned` re-judged fenced text, and at that point there was no `_owner` o … Breaks: Nothing functional. One edge case changes: a sheet outside #view that the observer never saw (not a direct child of head or body), judged invasive and then edited to clean by its app, now reads clean on a later ask instead of stale-invasive. That later ask only happens if the full load triggered by the first `true` was aborted.; A commit still needs its CHANGELOG.md and CHANGELOG_ru.md entry (repo rule). The comment at 202-204 must stay above the renamed function.

### `appearance-1-2` Порядок пунктов в селектах теряется: Object.keys ставит числовые ключи первыми ('2020' в Palette, у fs-select любое числовое значение)

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est 0 · changes behaviour

On 24.10, 25.12 and master, ui.RangeSlider.render() returns div.cbi-range-slider, with the input[type=range] as its first child and no aria-label. fs-appearance.js:290 puts the label on that div. The label.cbi-value-title at :256 has no `for` and does not wrap the control. No theme JS links labels, so all six sliders have no accessible name. Upstream gives the <select> the id `widget.<id>` and the frame div `<id>`, so `for=<id>` points at a div, which a label cannot name. group() is also shared by the colour rows (two inputs, already named at fs-appearance.js:144/147) and by the Saved-look button row, so one `for` per row does not fit.; Comments go stale. fs-appearance.js:249-251 and tools/playground/verify.mjs:162-165 describe the aria-label where it sits now, so the verify.mjs note becomes false once the fix lands.
- **Verdict (regression): holds.** The bug is real. It was a regression in 161a053: the old fs-widgets sliderControl put aria-label on the input[type=range] itself. When the code moved to ui.RangeSlider/ui.Select, the label landed on a generic div, which cannot carry a name, so the 6 range inputs have no accessible name. live-audit.mjs:268-269 misses this because it falls back to the value attribute. Variant 1 is safe on 24.10, 25.12 and master. Neither render() changed across them: firstElementChild is the input and the select. … Breaks: Functionally nothing. Stale claim: the comment at tools/playground/verify.mjs:162-166 says aria-label sits on the wrapping div, which is false after the fix. Rewrite or drop it in the same change.; Variant 2 (id plus label `for`) costs more code: ids must be unique on the page, and ui.Select gives the <select> the id `widget.<id>`, not `<id>`. The `for` on a select that fs-select hides points at a display:none element, and fs-select already focuses the widget when the title is clicked. No gain over variant 1.

- **Claim:** Пока ось выключена (0, следует палитре) или держит legacy-hue, reflect() кладёт в hex-поле вычисленный цвет палитры. commit() на blur/Enter видит валидный '#rrggbb' и вызывает pick(), то есть axis.apply(hex): ось становится явным hex. Достаточно табнуть/кликнуть через поле (или переключить окно, что тоже даёт blur) — ось пинится к цвету текущей палитры и режима: кнопка Palette включается, Save to router загорается без единой правки, а при последующем переключении в тёмный режим карточки остаются светлыми (#ffffff под светлым --fs-text). Если после этого нажать Save, этот пин уходит роутерным умолчанием на все браузеры. Legacy-hue Tint при этом молча превращается в hex.

Невалидный ввод после Enter откатывается на blur, как и сейчас: флаг сбрасывается только когда reflect действительно переписал поле.

- **Verdict (batch): holds.** Дефект есть: reflect() пишет цвет палитры в hex-поле, commit() на blur видит валидный #rrggbb и вызывает pick(), то есть axis.apply. Достаточно протабать через поле: ось пинится, legacy-hue Tint превращается в hex, загорается Save. Предложенная защита `v === swatch.value` закрывает это и сохраняет откат после Enter на невалидном вводе. Но с ней теряется одна возможность: набранный руками ровно показанный цвет палитры больше не закрепляется. Нативный пикер на тот же цвет тоже не шлёт input, так ч … Breaks: Набранный руками ровно показанный цвет палитры (например #ffffff в светлом режиме, чтобы карточки остались белыми и в тёмном) молча игнорируется; нативный пикер на тот же цвет input не шлёт, так что закрепить точный цвет палитры больше нечем

So the contrast readouts for Accent, Good, Warn, Danger and Borders (measured on var(--fs-panel)), plus the Sidebar row's hex and contrast (var(--fs-bar-bg) = var(--fs-panel) while the bar axis is off and the palette is not forum), stay stale. Card is the only axis other rows depend on. The proposal's second half, dropping reflect(v) from pick, breaks … Breaks: Storage-blocked browser, no router default for the axis: after any swatch or field pick, the edited row's Palette button turns disabled (current() returns 0), so the user cannot send that axis back to the palette.; Storage-blocked browser, router default is a hex h: on every swatch `input` event the swatch and field are reset to h while the page is painted in the picked colour, so the native picker fights the user. Palette (pick(0)) leaves the swatch showing h and the button enabled over a page painted in the palette colour.; est_lines_saved=1 is wrong. The fix is a one-token change and saves nothing.
- **Verdict (regression): holds.** The bug is real. CARD sets --fs-panel-base (fs-axes.js:194). --fs-panel is var(--fs-panel-base) (03-palettes.css:15), and --fs-bar-bg is var(--fs-panel) (02-tokens.css:64; only the forum palette overrides it, at :280). pick only reflects its own row (fs-appearance.js:191). Under prefers-contrast:more, Tint also moves --fs-border (95-a11y-media.css:25). The proposal as written has one regression. It drops the self reflect(v), so the row re-reads o.read(). When localStorage is blocked, lsSet swall … Breaks: Blocked-storage mode, which the page supports (prefs.storageBroken(), fs-appearance.js:626-631, says changes last until reload). fs-prefs.js:30-31 swallow the localStorage error, and lsGet returns null. Dropping the self reflect(v) makes the picked row re-read axis.current(), which falls back to def() (the router default, usually 0). The swatch and hex field show the palette's colour, the 'Palette' button disables, and the page stays painted in the picked colour. This inverts the invariant at :195-196 ('the field cannot claim a colour the page is not painted in'). On blur commit the field is no longer activeElement, so the typed hex is overwritten. While the native picker is dragged, swatch.value is reset to the default on every input event.

### `fit-1-11` Comments in fs-chrome.js state mechanisms the code does not have

**confirmed** · false-claim · risk low · est 3

- **Claim:** (1) :152 says 'the gutter is re-asked even on a memo hit', but :153 returns before any gutter read, and the gutter only arrives through measureShell's side-write at :224. (2) :583-586 and docs/chrome.md:113 say a resize starts the scrolling() window because 'fs-fit.js's resize observer feeds the same motion sampler'. onResize (fs-fit.js:239-249) only bumps _resizeSeq and calls schedule(), and _movingUntil is written only from the scroll/wheel/touchmove path (fs-fit.js:181,205). (3) :398-401 says 'No observer ... of our own — fs-fit owns both', but :558 creates a MutationObserver that calls fitChrome(). (4) :285-289 and docs/chrome.md:142 say WebKit has no scroll anchoring at all, which docs/anchoring.md:17,27 contradicts (WebKit 26 anchors, all three engines answer true). (5) :132-135 says density is 'the one thing' that keys the memo, while :146-151 adds a second key (itself dead; see the data-content-width bug). (6) :139-141 says the constant saved 23 B. Terser measures 26 B, and under jsmin (luci.mk's node-less path, conventions.md:178), which does not rename identifiers, it costs about +45 B.

It is not a defect. (2) fs-chrome.js:583-586 and docs/chrome.md:113: drop the claim that the ResizeObserver feeds the sampler. Say that the window opens on any scroll event the theme did not write, including one a resize causes by moving the offset (fs-fit.js:203-205,222). onResize (:239-249) only schedules. (3) fs-chrome.js:398-401: name wireIndicatorCounts' MutationObserver (:558-562) as the one fitChrome() trigger outside fs-fit, and drop the '(docs/conventions.md)' pointer while editing. (4) fs-chrome.js:285-289 is self-contradictory ('WebKit's own scroll anchoring' vs 'no anchoring at all'). Rewrite it and docs/chrome.md:142 to 'Safari before 26 has no scroll anchoring' (consistent with anchoring.md:17,27). Also anchoring-log.md:36 says the same thing. (5) fs-chrome.js:132-135: drop 'the one thing'. The real fix belongs to the separate data-content-width memo-key bug: nothing writes data-content-width, and propAxis sets --fs-content-max inline (fs-axes.js:99-105,215). Also fix fs-axes.js:210-211 ('reads --fs-content-max on every fit'), which is false under the memo. (6) fs-chrome.js:139-141: keep the constant. Either drop the byte parenthetical or state it as 'terser: 26 B saved; jsmin: +45 B'.
- **Original proposal:** Correct or delete each sentence in the edit that touches it. (1) becomes true with the gutter refactor. For (2), say a resize mid-flick lands inside a window that a scroll event opened. For (3), name the indicator observer as the one exception. For (4), align with docs/anchoring.md. For (6), drop the byte claim or inline the literal like 'fs-bar-stack' and 'fs-bar-actrow', which are repeated just as often.
- **Verdict (combined): holds.** Five of the six sites are confirmed at 8e33fb3. Site (1) is not false. Both callers run measureShell() before shellGeometry() (fs-chrome.js:243→248 and :598→600). measureShell() writes the gutter into _geom at :224, and a memo miss restores it at :182. So a memo hit does return a gutter that was just re-asked; the comment only sits in a misleading spot. The proposal touches only comments and docs, so nothing functional can break. Two parts need a fix. In (2), the wording "mid-flick" is too narro … Breaks: (6) The inline option adds 26 B to the terser build that release CI ships (6784 -> 6810 B). ### `menu-1-2` clampDropdown does nothing in RTL, so a bar panel can hang off the left edge

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est -2 · changes behaviour

- **Where:** luci-theme-footstrap/htdocs/luci-static/resources/menu-footstrap.js:96-121; luci-theme-footstrap/styles/theme/20-shell.css:108
- **Claim:** The bar panel is anchored with `inset-inline: 0 auto`, which is right:0 under dir=rtl (head.ut:136 sets dir from _rtl). Its right edge is then always its item's right edge, which is on screen, so `r.right - (innerWidth - EDGE_GAP)` is never positive and nothing gets clamped. The overflow in RTL goes past the LEFT edge, and no code checks for it. Arabic, Hebrew and Persian users get panels clipped off-screen near the inline end of the bar, the mirror of the LTR case the function exists to fix.
- **Proposal:** Apply as written, inside the rAF in clampDropdown: ``` menu.style.insetInlineStart = ''; const r = …; if (!r.width) return; const rtl = getComputedStyle(menu).direction === 'rtl'; const over = rtl ? EDGE_GAP - r.left : r.right - (innerWidth - EDGE_GAP); if (over > 0) menu.style.insetInlineStart = -Math.min(over, rtl ? innerWidth - EDGE_GAP - r.right : r.left - EDGE_GAP) + 'px'; ``` clearClamps resets `m.style.insetInlineStart = ''`. Using `document.documentElement.dir === 'rtl'` is equivalent and skips a style lookup. In the same change, update the comments at menu-footstrap.js:83-85, 20-shell.css:103-104 and docs/chrome.md:228/:332 to say 'inline-end edge'. Add the CHANGELOG.md + CHANGELOG_ru.md entry.
- **Original proposal:** Clamp on the inline-end edge through the logical property. Set `const rtl = getComputedStyle(menu).direction === 'rtl'`. Then `over = rtl ? EDGE_GAP - r.left : r.right - (innerWidth - EDGE_GAP)` and `room = rtl ? innerWidth - EDGE_GAP - r.right : r.left - EDGE_GAP`. If over > 0, set `menu.style.insetInlineStart = -Math.min(over, room) + 'px'`. Reset `style.insetInlineStart` instead of `style.left` in both clampDropdown and clearClamps.
- **Verdict (reality): holds.** The defect exists at HEAD. head.ut:136 writes dir=rtl for ar/fa/he etc. 20-shell.css:108 `inset-inline: 0 auto` resolves to right:0 under RTL, so the panel's right edge sits on its item's right edge, and that edge is at least 16px inside the viewport because of the bar padding. That makes `overflowRight` at menu-footstrap.js:112 always <= -8 in RTL, and nothing checks the left edge. Even if the clamp did fire, an inline `left` together with right:0 and width:max-content is over-constrained, and … Breaks: Nothing breaks functionally. LTR results are the same in every modelled case. `style.insetInlineStart` needs the same browser floor as the `inset-inline` shorthand the panel already depends on.; As written, the proposal leaves comments stating the old rule: menu-footstrap.js:83-85 ('ul left:0', 'near the right edge'), 20-shell.css:103-104 ('near the right edge') and docs/chrome.md:332 ('at the right edge'). All three must change with the code.
- **Verdict (regression): holds.** The bug is real. head.ut:136 sets dir=rtl for ar/fa/he etc., 20-shell.css:108 anchors the panel with `inset-inline: 0 auto` (right:0 in RTL), and the bar is a flex row with nothing forcing LTR. The panel's right edge therefore sits on its item and the only check, r.right overflow, can never fire. The proposal reproduces the LTR result exactly, because inset-inline-start maps to left in LTR with the same value. I found no consumer of style.left, no test, no gate and no physical left/right/transla … Breaks: Nothing functional. The text the change leaves stale is the menu-footstrap.js:83-85 header ('ul left:0', 'near the right edge'), the 20-shell.css:103-104 comment ('near the right edge'), and docs/chrome.md:332 and :228 ('at the right edge'). Each should say the inline-end edge.

Output: 'ltr panel 300..520 nudge -138 -> visible from 162' and 'rtl panel -130..90 nudge 0 -> visible from -130'. 20-shell.css:108 is `position: absolute; inset-inline: 0 auto;`. The only correction is `menu.style.left`, a physical property, and it only handles the right edge.

### `menu-1-3` Search trigger and shortcuts are bound twice, with a pending/loaded flag pair between the copies

**refuted** · duplication · risk low · est 28

- **Where:** menu-footstrap-common.js:105-131; fs-search.js:166-168, 331, 338-352, 357-365
- **Claim:** common binds the button click and Ctrl/Cmd+K and `/` until fs-search loads. Then fs-search binds its own button toggle and its own copy of the same keydown handler, with the identical guard selector 'input, textarea, select, [contenteditable], .cbi-dropdown'. A `pending` and a `loaded` flag keep the two owners from fighting; commit 1f9dade recorded that they did fight (open/open/open). The palette's only caller is common, so one owner is enough. fs-search's `if (!btn) return null` and `if (_built)` guards are also dead, because common.wireSearch dereferences the same button unconditionally (btn.addEventListener) before the module can ever load.
- **Proposal:** fs-search.build() returns {open, close, toggle: () => (ov.hidden ? open() : close())}. Export `open` and `toggle` from a lazily built singleton. Delete fs-search.js:331 (btn listener), 338-352 (document keydown) and the null-btn guards. In common, keep one click listener and one keydown listener permanently and drop pending/loaded: `const palette = (fn) => RT.require('fs-search').then((m) => m[fn](), (e) => console.error('footstrap: fs-search did not load', e));` Click and Ctrl/Cmd+K call palette('toggle'); `/` calls palette('open').
- **Verdict (combined): refuted.** The facts hold at HEAD. common binds the click, Ctrl/Cmd+K and `/`, fs-search binds its own copies, and the null-btn guard is dead. ### `templates-1-11` The 'CI compiles every .ut' claim skips partials/: the trycompile glob does not recurse

**confirmed** · false-claim · risk low · est 0

- **Where:** .github/workflows/build.yml:186, 201; tools/ci-local.sh:266; docs/architecture.md:65-67; .claude/rules/chrome.md ('full sweep over every installed template')
- **Claim:** The verify step runs `ucode -T -c` over `/usr/share/ucode/luci/template/themes/footstrap/*.ut`, which covers header.ut, footer.ut and sysauth.ut only. The seven partials are never compiled by that assertion. The `http 200 …/overview` assertion does render every partial (noscript renders notice.ut, the rail toggle renders icon.ut), so coverage exists, but indirectly and not where the docs say. LuCI's trycompile also compiles only header.ut: a broken partial gives a 500 on every page instead of a theme fallback.
- **Proposal:** Prefer widening the glob over rewording five doc sentences. It is one token per site, and it makes every existing 'every template' sentence true. In build.yml:186,201, ci-local.sh:266 and the doc copies at docs/ci.md:235 and docs/development.md:678,685, change `for f in $UT/*.ut` to `for f in $UT/*.ut $UT/partials/*.ut`, the same form development.md:739 already uses. Benefit: a stripped partial (strip-templates.sh rewrites partials too) now fails as a named compile error rather than a bare 500 on overview. No doc rewrite is needed beyond the glob copies.
- **Original proposal:** Change the glob to `…/footstrap/*.ut …/footstrap/partials/*.ut` in both the workflow and ci-local.sh, or correct the two docs to say partials are covered by the render assertion.
- **Verdict (combined): holds.** Confirmed at HEAD. The verify glob `themes/footstrap/*.ut` matches header, footer and sysauth only. The 7 partials are never compiled by it. Their coverage comes indirectly from `http 200 …/overview`: owlab logs in, and all 7 partials load unconditionally under !blank_page (header.ut:138-209, with notice.ut reached through <noscript>). A compile error in a partial goes loadfile → render_any die → error500, so the page returns 500, not a theme fallback (runtime.uc:158 trycompiles only the header, … Breaks: Nothing functional. The finding's touch list misses the doc sites that mirror the glob or repeat the claim: docs/ci.md:235, docs/development.md:208,678,685 and docs/conventions.md:420. ci.md also says to keep owlab-test docs and CI 'in step', so changing only build.yml and ci-local.sh leaves development.md:678,685 stale.

### `templates-1-6` Footer forces a contentinfo landmark inside <main> (axe landmark-contentinfo-is-top-level)

**refuted** · bug · risk low · est 7 · changes behaviour

- **Where:** footer.ut:9-16; docs/chrome.md:291-293
- **Claim:** `<footer class="fs-footer" role="contentinfo">` sits inside `<main class="fs-main">` (header.ut:189, footer.ut:29). The explicit role puts a contentinfo landmark inside the main landmark. ARIA expects contentinfo at top level, and axe flags this exact shape. The comment justifies the role by the fact that the implicit mapping is lost inside <main>, and that loss is the spec telling you this is not page-level contentinfo.
- **Proposal:** Drop `role="contentinfo"` and the 6-line comment, leaving a plain footer that is generic inside main. The alternative, moving <footer> after </main> inside .fs-shell, needs CSS changes to the flex order. Fix docs/chrome.md:291-293.
- **Verdict (reality): refuted.** The axe flag is real: the `landmark-contentinfo-is-top-level` rule (axe 4.12.1) matches an explicit role and fails it when any ancestor is a landmark. But it is a best-practice rule of moderate impact, not a WCAG failure. The role was added on purpose in 9c90db4 so the footer counts as a landmark, and browsers do expose an explicit role that sits inside main. Dropping it takes away the only contentinfo landmark, so screen-reader users lose a landmark they can jump to. That breaks "zero functiona … Breaks: Removes the page's only contentinfo landmark: screen-reader landmark navigation (NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver) can no longer jump to the footer, a regression from 9c90db4's deliberate a11y fix and from parity with upstream bootstrap, which ships an implicit top-level contentinfo; Dropping 'the 6-line comment' wholesale deletes footer.ut:13-14, the entityencode rationale for the version strings, which is unrelated to the role; The alternative (footer after </main>) breaks sidebar layout: .fs-shell is a flex row with overflow:hidden (20-shell.css:220-221), so the footer would become a side column, and 20-shell.css:545 ordering after prepended alerts would be lost
- **Verdict (regression): refuted.** The axe claim holds. landmark-contentinfo-is-top-level matches this footer, and the markup also breaks aria-allowed-role, because footer's allowedRoles do not include contentinfo. Both rules carry the best-practice tag, not a WCAG one. Dropping the role still removes the only contentinfo landmark on the page. Commit 9c90db4 added that landmark on purpose as an a11y fix. With the role gone, screen-reader users can no longer jump to the footer (version info) through landmark navigation (NVDA/JAWS … Breaks: Removes the page's only contentinfo landmark: screen-reader landmark navigation (NVDA D, JAWS R/;, VoiceOver rotor) can no longer reach the footer/version line. This reverts a deliberate a11y fix from commit 9c90db4.; It exchanges a working landmark for passing an axe best-practice rule that no gate runs (a11y-gallery.mjs runs WCAG tags only, over the gallery, which has no chrome). That is a loss of protection, not a defect fix.; The suggested alternative (moving footer after </main>) breaks the sidebar layout: .fs-shell is a 100svh flex row with overflow:hidden and .fs-main is the scroller (20-shell.css:220-227). The footer would become a third column, would not scroll with content, and would invalidate the anchor that tools/table-tick.mjs:26,74,96 relies on.

### `tools-anchor-1-4` scroll-anchor drives the owlab -b twins without taking their stand lock

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est -2 · changes behaviour

- **Where:** tools/scroll-anchor.mjs:1116-1124, 1484-1497; tools/lib/stands.mjs:195-210 (pairStands), 283-290 (requireStands)
- **Claim:** requireStands() flocks only the base list (CORE: owrt2512/owrt2410/owrtsnap). pairStands() then adds each running `-b` twin as a second worker, and runCell measures on twin.base with no lock on the twin. The lock exists because two runs on one stand invent findings (stands.mjs:212-215). owlab.yaml:220 says the `-b` set exists for contention between two people, so a twin in use by another session is driven unlocked. docs/development.md:1670-1682 also records the result: a different build's half-sweep gets reported under the base stand's name.
- **Proposal:** Keep the base lock blocking and make the twin lock try-only. scroll-anchor.mjs: ``` let list = stands(FLAGS.only, { all: FLAGS.all }); if (QUICK && !FLAGS.only) list = list.slice(0, 1); requireStands(list, 'scroll-anchor'); const PAIRS = FLAGS['no-pair'] ? new Map() : pairStands(list, 'scroll-anchor'); ``` This keeps the slice before the lock, so --quick no longer locks stands it then discards. stands.mjs: - Factor the spawn/ack loop in lockStands into `take(id, name, wait)`. - With wait=false, spawn `sh -c 'flock -n -x "$2" sh -c "echo \"$1\" >\"$2\"; echo ok; cat >/dev/null" sh "$1" "$2" || echo busy'` and poll the ack for ok/busy. The scratch prototype trylock.mjs proves this pattern. - In pairStands, add the twin only if heldBy(twinId) is true or take(twinId, name, false) succeeds. Otherwise print `<name>: twin <id> is in use (<holder>); measuring <base> alone` to stderr. Effect: twin locks never wait, so no deadlock and no 30-min stall. The twin is held for the run, and every cell still runs once on the base (development.md:436-437). Update development.md:433-438 ('up and not locked'), fix the stale :164 pointer at :1672, and fix the :985-987 lock-file name. Net change is about +8 lines, not -2.
- **Original proposal:** Pair only twins this process can lock. Reorder to `let list = stands(...); if (QUICK && !FLAGS.only) list = list.slice(0,1); const PAIRS = …pairStands(list); requireStands([...list, ...PAIRS.values()], 'scroll-anchor')`, or drop a twin whose `flock -n` fails instead of waiting on it. This also stops --quick from locking stands it then discards.
- **Verdict (reality): holds.** The core claim holds at HEAD. requireStands() locks only the stands() list (tools/scroll-anchor.mjs:1116). pairStands() (stands.mjs:198-210) adds running `<id>b` twins and takes no lock, and :1485 drives twin.base. ci-local's anchors leg has the same gap: it locks only $ROUTERS and passes --only owrt2512, so the twin is still paired and stays unlocked. The --quick side bug is also real: :1116 locks all CORE stands and :1120 then keeps one. The proposal's main form is wrong, though. If the twin i … Breaks: With the primary form (lock twins through requireStands), a twin held by another session makes scroll-anchor wait up to STANDS_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS (30 min) and then exit 2. Today the run proceeds. The twin is optional concurrency and should never block or fail the run.; Claiming that this fixes the docs/development.md:1670-1682 'twin runs a different build' trap would be wrong. A lock does not make the twin carry this session's build.
- **Verdict (regression): holds.** The bug is real. requireStands (scroll-anchor.mjs:1116) locks only the base ids. pairStands (stands.mjs:198-210) then adds running -b twins with no lock, and the twin is driven at :1485. owlab.yaml:220 confirms the twins exist for another person to use. Of the two fixes offered, the blocking one, requireStands([...list, ...twins]), breaks things. A busy twin is an optional speed-up, yet it would stall the run for up to 30 min and then exit 2. Under ci-local it also adds a second lock phase that … Breaks: Blocking variant: another session's sweep holding owrt2512b now makes a plain `npm run anchor` wait for it. It waits up to 30 min (stands.mjs:258-263), then exits 2. The twin is an optional speed-up (docs/development.md:433-438), and the base alone could have finished the run cleanly.; Blocking variant under tools/ci-local.sh: ci-local first locks owrt2410, owrt2512 and owrtsnap on fds 9-7 (:421-431). Its child scroll-anchor then blocks on a twin. Meanwhile a gate run as `--only owrt2512b,owrtsnap` holds owrt2512b and waits on owrtsnap. The sorted lock order no longer prevents deadlock, because locks are taken in two phases. Both processes stall for 30 min, then exit 2.; Reorder variant as written: PAIRS is computed before requireStands, which may wait up to 30 min for the bases. A twin that goes down during the wait is still handed work, and its cells are logged as 'never opened' (unopened tolerance).; est_lines_saved -2 is wrong. lockStands has no non-blocking path, and the event loop is blocked while it waits, so a `flock -n` exit is never seen. A try-lock needs its own ack signal ('ok'/'busy'), about 8 lines. A spawnSync probe with `flock -n file true` has a check-then-use race and holds nothing for the rest of the run.; Docs: development.md:433-438 would need 'up and free'. development.md:1672 points at stands.mjs:164, which is stale (pairStands is now at :198). development.md:985-987 describes `stands-<set>.lock`, but the code locks per id (`stands-<id>.lock`).

### `tools-anchor-2-3` SWAP's floor-only pass is measured against the baseline taken before the first pass, so the first pass's leftover offset is blamed on the floor

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est -1 · changes behaviour

- **Where:** tools/scroll-anchor.mjs:591 (before, taken once), 605-609, 644, 681, 688-689 (swap() reads the outer before.pos/before.top), 686-687 (pass 1 removes its pad and waits; this is never measured), 699-703 (second swap()), 1390-1392 (floorClamped judged), 1439-1441 (printed)
- **Claim:** swap() runs twice: corrected, then with fsAnchor=off. Both runs compute moved, clamped (`before.pos - empty.pos`), offsetDelta and correctedAt against the single `before` captured before pass 1. Between the passes, pass 1 removes its 120px pad from a body above the reader, which shrinks the page above the reader, and waits 700ms. Nothing measures whether that shrink was corrected. Any offset it leaves is added to pass 2's `clamped`/`moved`. On the noEngineAnchor cell that becomes the finding 'the engine clamped Npx away — the content column's floor is not holding the document up', which charges a correction fault to the floor. This has been the design since d0445ce, which introduced the second pass.
- **Proposal:** Как предложено: первой строкой swap() снять const base = { pos: pos(), top: mark.isConnected ? Math.round(mark.getBoundingClientRect().top) : null } и внутри swap() (read(), offsetDelta, moved, clamped) использовать base вместо before. Остаток между проходами вернуть отдельным полем и печатать рядом с 'floor alone': return { ..., drift: base.pos - before.pos }.
- **Original proposal:** At the top of swap(), take `const base = { pos: pos(), top: mark.isConnected ? Math.round(mark.getBoundingClientRect().top) : null }` and use it in place of `before` inside swap(). Pass 1 does not change, because base equals before at that moment. Pass 2 is then judged on its own refill only. If the leftover between passes is worth reporting, return `base.pos - before.pos` as its own printed number.
- **Verdict (batch): holds.** Подтверждено. Оба прохода swap() считают moved, clamped, offsetDelta и correctedAt от одного before, снятого до первого прохода. Между проходами pad.remove() сжимает тело над читателем (body выбран целиком выше вьюпорта, :508-509), затем wait(700), и остаток L ничем не измеряется. clamped_2 = L + реальный clamp, так что L>0 ложно записывается полу, а L<0 маскирует настоящий clamp. Такой остаток виден в логе: 'floor alone: clamped -120px' (anchoring-log.md:894). Для первого прохода base совпадает …

### `tools-static-1-1` page-modules не видит третье сравнение data-page в fs-overview.js (комментарий между !== и литералом)

**confirmed** · bug · risk low · est 1 · changes behaviour

- **Where:** tools/page-modules.mjs:33-38; luci-theme-footstrap/htdocs/luci-static/resources/fs-overview.js:151-153
- **Claim:** Гейт ищет значения data-page тремя regex по сырому тексту модуля. Если там опечатка, гейт остаётся зелёным, а модуль на своей странице вызывает stopWatch(). Первый regex (`const PAGE = '…'`) не совпадает ни с одним файлом в resources/, а третий дублирует второй.

KEEP line 37 (the getAttribute regex; it catches a typo in the 'admin-' prefix itself) and KEEP line 38 (the [!=]== 'admin-…' regex; it catches comparisons written without getAttribute). Delete only line 36 (const PAGE): it is dead at HEAD, and a module that hoisted the value would now fail loudly with "nothing in it tests a data-page value", which matches docs/development.md:1214. Update the stale comments: :5-9 (fs-appearance is no longer a page module) and :34 ("a PAGE constant… fs-overview does both" is false). fs-overview.js needs no change; the comment at :151-152 becomes true. Net lines saved: about 0. The value of the change is the fixed gap, not the size.
- **Original proposal:** В цикле по модулям сначала убирать комментарии: `const text = src(name + '.js').replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, ' ')`. Оставить один regex `getAttribute\('data-page'\)[^;]{0,40}?[!=]==\s*'([a-z0-9-]+)'`, а строки 36 и 38 удалить. Обновить заголовок (:5): fs-appearance больше не page-модуль.
- **Verdict (reality): holds.** The bug is real at HEAD. fs-overview.js has three data-page comparisons: :151-153, :237 and :243. At :151-153 a block comment sits between `!==` and the literal, so none of the three regexes in tools/page-modules.mjs:36-38 matches it. The comment came in with ed525b3. A typo at :153 keeps the gate green while arrange() calls stopWatch() on the overview, so the grid is never arranged. The proposal (strip comments, keep one getAttribute regex) runs and turns red on a mutation at each of the three … Breaks: Dropping regex :38 (`[!=]==\s*'(admin-…)'`) is a narrowing, not a pure duplicate. It is the only regex that catches a comparison spelled without getAttribute, such as `dataset.page === 'admin-x'` or `p !== 'admin-x'`. HEAD has no such site, so nothing breaks today. A module that uses only that spelling would fail loudly ('nothing in it tests'). A module that mixes spellings would be missed silently.; The proposal updates the header at :5 but leaves :33-34 '(fs-overview does both)' / 'a PAGE constant', which becomes false once regex :36 is gone. That comment also has to change.
- **Verdict (regression): holds.** The bug is real. At fs-overview.js:151-153 a /* */ comment sits between `!==` and the literal, so none of the three regexes sees that comparison. A typo there leaves the gate green, and arrange() then calls stopWatch() on the overview page. Stripping comments first fixes it. Deleting regex 3 (page-modules.mjs:38), as proposed, loses coverage the gate has today: a comparison written without getAttribute (dataset.page, or a variable holding the attribute) with a wrong value is caught now and would … Breaks: Deleting regex 3 (tools/page-modules.mjs:38) stops the gate catching a comparison written without getAttribute('data-page') right before it, e.g. `document.body.dataset.page === 'admin-x'` or `const p = …getAttribute('data-page'); if (p !== 'admin-x')`. When another comparison in the same module is caught, the wrong value passes. The current gate catches it (simulated: cur FAIL, prop PASS).
